title: Accorder et écrire les descriptions
summary: Handle -u and -al adjective forms, colour agreement, de before plural adjectives and selected -ément adverbs.
objectives: Form feminine -u and masculine plural -al adjectives with common exceptions.
Distinguish variable simple colours from invariable compound and noun-based colours.
Use pre-noun de and memorized -ément adverbs.

sources.label: University of Texas: irregular adjective agreement
Wiktionary: final, including both plural forms
Wiktionary: banal, ordinary and historical meanings
OQLF: traditional and rectified diaeresis spellings
OQLF: coordinated colour adjectives and accepted agreement

sections.title: Regular feminine -ue; a plural -al family
paragraphs: An adjective ending in -u normally adds e in the feminine without changing the spoken ending: pointu/pointue, têtu/têtue, inconnu/inconnue. Full agreement is pointu, pointue, pointus, pointues. Do not confuse these with adjectives ending in -eux, which follow another pattern.

Most -al adjectives have masculine plural -aux and feminine -ale/-ales: original, originale, originaux, originales; national, nationale, nationaux, nationales. Common masculine -als exceptions include banal in its ordinary commonplace meaning, bancal, fatal, natal and naval. Final accepts finals and finaux; idéal accepts idéals and idéaux. Glacial also has glacials/glaciaux, depending on usage. Do not mark the accepted second forms wrong.

Banaux exists in the historical feudal sense of banal, relating to a lord's shared facilities; it is not the ordinary plural for commonplace remarks. This is recognition vocabulary, not a required productive historical register. Vocabulary: un propos (masculine), a remark; un chantier (masculine), a worksite; une table (feminine), a table.
points: The -al exceptions concern masculine plurals; feminine plurals still end in -ales: navales, banales, finales.
Learn an unfamiliar -al adjective with its dictionary plural instead of assuming every adjective follows one pattern.

examples.note: Inconnu gains e for feminine réponse.

examples.french: Ces idées sont **originales**, et ces dessins sont **originaux**.
examples.english: These ideas are original, and these drawings are original.
We are waiting for the final results.
examples.note: Both masculine plural forms are accepted.

mistakes.why: Feminine plural réponses requires originales, not masculine originaux.

sections.title: A colour phrase is not always an ordinary adjective
paragraphs: Simple colour adjectives normally agree: bleu/bleue/bleus/bleues, vert/verte/verts/vertes. A compound shade normally stays unchanged as a whole: bleu clair, vert foncé, bleu marine. Do not add plural s to either part just because the noun is plural.

Many colours taken from object names stay unchanged: orange, marron, crème. Established adjective exceptions do agree, including rose, mauve, pourpre, écarlate, fauve and incarnat. Thus roses but rose pâle when a compound shade is intended. A mixed shade formed from two basic colours can be hyphenated, such as bleu-vert, and stays invariable. Vocabulary: une écharpe (feminine), a scarf; un rideau (masculine), a curtain.
points: The rule concerns use as a colour description: the fruit noun une orange can of course have plural oranges.
Do not infer a colour's agreement solely from its historical origin; learn the established exceptions.

examples.note: Marron is invariable as a colour adjective.

examples.french: Nous avons choisi des rideaux **bleu clair**.
Les fleurs **roses** sont près des fleurs **orange**.
examples.english: The pink flowers are next to the orange flowers.
examples.note: Rose agrees; orange does not in this colour use.

mistakes.why: For the single compound shade dark green, both words remain unchanged.

sections.title: Two small changes around descriptions
paragraphs: In careful French, plural indefinite des normally becomes de/d' before an adjective placed before its noun: de longues tables, d'excellentes idées. Des remains normal when the adjective follows the noun: des tables longues. Fixed noun groups such as des petits pois (peas) and des grands-parents keep des; spoken usage also often keeps des before a free adjective. This rule is not about du or de la.

Some common adverbs are learned with -ément rather than by mechanically adding -ment to a feminine adjective: énorme gives énormément (a great deal), précis gives précisément (precisely), profond gives profondément (deeply), intense gives intensément (intensely), aveugle gives aveuglément (blindly), commun gives communément (commonly), confus gives confusément (vaguely/confusedly) and commode gives commodément (conveniently). Conforme gives conformément (in accordance), and exprès gives expressément (expressly). Adverbs do not agree with a noun or subject.
points: Do not invent a general rule that every adjective can take -ément.
Vocabulary: un petit pois (masculine), a pea; les grands-parents (masculine plural), grandparents. The family term is a fixed noun group.

examples.note: Des becomes d' before the preceding adjective.

examples.french: Elle a répondu **précisément** à la question.
examples.note: The adverb describes the answering and does not agree with elle.
Profondément has an accented é before -ment.

sections.title: Distinguer les finales en -u et le tréma
paragraphs: The ordinary feminine ending -ue remains right for pointu and têtu. A smaller spelling family needs a diaeresis, the two dots indicating that a vowel must be pronounced separately: aigu, ambigu, contigu and exigu. When e is added after gu, the spelling must still show that the u is heard. Do not extend the dots to every adjective ending in -u.

Both traditional and rectified spellings are standard: aigu / aiguë or aigüe / aigus / aiguës or aigües; ambigu / ambiguë or ambigüe / ambigus / ambiguës or ambigües; contigu / contiguë or contigüe / contigus / contiguës or contigües; exigu / exiguë or exigüe / exigus / exiguës or exigües. Each sequence gives masculine singular, feminine singular, masculine plural, feminine plural. The feminine does not gain an extra spoken syllable merely because an e is written.
points: Aigu can mean sharp or high-pitched; ambigu means ambiguous; contigu means adjoining; exigu means cramped. Vocabulary: une consigne (feminine), an instruction; une pièce (feminine), a room.
The OQLF accepts both traditional and rectified spellings; the exercises accept both positions of the diaeresis, but not its omission.

examples.french: La consigne est **ambiguë / ambigüe** : faut-il signer ou seulement lire ?
examples.english: The instruction is ambiguous: should we sign or only read?
examples.note: The ambiguity concerns the required action. The two spellings represent the same pronunciation.

examples.french: Ces pièces **exiguës / exigües** ne conviennent pas aux réunions.
examples.english: These cramped rooms are unsuitable for meetings.
examples.note: The feminine plural needs e, the diaeresis and plural s.

examples.french: Une sonnerie **aiguë / aigüe** retentit dans les deux salles **contiguës / contigües**.
examples.english: A high-pitched ringing sounds in the two adjoining rooms.
examples.note: Apply the same spelling principle independently to a singular and a plural adjective.

mistakes.why: The pronounced u needs a diaeresis in this feminine form. Ambigüe is equally correct; plain ambigue is not the standard spelling.

sections.title: Identifier la construction avant de modifier un mot
paragraphs: Two different constructions happen to be written des. The indefinite article in des objets means some objects; before a freely added adjective, careful writing uses de beaux objets. But de + les also contracts to des. If a verb or expression already requires de and the following noun group is definite, keep des even before an adjective: parler des nouvelles mesures means to discuss the new measures. Ask first whether you mean some or of/about/from the.

A colour qualifier can be a noun, not just clair or foncé: bleu marine stays unchanged as a shade. Do not treat marine as an extra agreeing adjective. In a phrase such as des fanions rouge et blanc, the invariable colour group can describe each pennant as having both colours. Agreement is also accepted for that multicolour reading: des fanions rouges et blancs. If the collection instead contains separate single-coloured objects, the adjectives agree. Consequently, an agreeing spelling alone does not always reveal the distribution; describe the pattern explicitly when it matters.

Uniforme gives the adverb uniformément, evenly or uniformly. The accent belongs to the learned adverb, not to an agreement ending. An adverb describing how material is distributed stays the same for any gender or number of material.
points: Vocabulary: une mesure (feminine), a measure; un fanion (masculine), a pennant; une housse (feminine), a cover.

examples.french: Le comité propose **de nouvelles mesures**, puis discute **des nouvelles mesures**.
examples.english: The committee proposes some new measures, then discusses the new measures.
examples.note: The first phrase introduces measures; the second uses discuter de + les to refer to the identified measures.

examples.french: Nous avons commandé des housses **bleu marine**.
Chaque bateau porte des fanions **rouge et blanc / rouges et blancs**.
examples.note: Each pennant has both colours in this description; either spelling is accepted.

examples.french: Répartissez la colle **uniformément** sur la surface.
examples.english: Spread the glue evenly over the surface.
examples.note: The adverb describes the spreading, not the feminine noun la colle, glue.

practice.prompt: Supply pointu in the correct form: une extrémité ___.
practice.explanation: Add e to -u for a feminine singular noun.

practice.prompt: Supply national in the correct form: des journaux ___.
practice.explanation: Masculine plural national becomes nationaux.

practice.prompt: Supply the colour marron after des chaussures.
practice.explanation: Marron stays invariable as a colour.

practice.prompt: Supply the careful-written indefinite article: Elle a ___ bonnes idées.
practice.explanation: Des becomes de before a preceding adjective.

practice.prompt: Supply têtu in the correct form: Ces deux femmes sont ___.
practice.explanation: Feminine plural adds -es to têtu.

practice.prompt: Supply original in the correct form: des projets ___.
practice.explanation: The masculine plural follows -al to -aux.

practice.prompt: Supply banal in its ordinary commonplace sense: des commentaires ___.
practice.explanation: Ordinary banal takes banals; banaux belongs to a historical sense.

practice.prompt: Supply final in the masculine plural: les résultats ___. Both standard plurals are accepted.
practice.explanation: Final has two accepted masculine plural forms.

practice.prompt: Supply the compound shade bleu clair after des vestes.
practice.explanation: A compound shade does not agree.

practice.prompt: Supply rose as a simple colour after des chemises.
practice.explanation: Rose is an established variable colour adjective.

practice.prompt: Give the adverb formed from précis meaning precisely.
practice.explanation: This learned form uses -ément.

practice.prompt: Supply de, d' or des in careful writing: Nous avons ___ excellentes nouvelles.
practice.explanation: De elides before the vowel of the preceding adjective.

practice.prompt: Supply naval in the correct form: des exercices ___.
practice.explanation: Naval is a common -als exception.

practice.prompt: Supply orange as a colour after des sacs.
practice.explanation: Orange remains invariable when naming the colour.

practice.prompt: Give the adverb formed from profond meaning deeply.
practice.explanation: Profondément has é before -ment.

practice.prompt: Choose the article for the established food name meaning peas: Nous achetons ___ petits pois.
practice.explanation: Petits pois is a fixed noun group, not a freely added adjective.

practice.prompt: Supply bancal in the correct form: Ces raisonnements sont ___.
practice.explanation: Bancal is a masculine -als exception, including this figurative use meaning shaky.

practice.prompt: Supply fatal in the correct form: des défauts ___ au projet.
practice.explanation: Fatal takes masculine plural fatals.

practice.prompt: Supply natal in the correct form: Ils retournent dans leurs villages ___.
practice.explanation: Natal takes -s, not -aux, in the masculine plural.

practice.prompt: Supply idéal in the masculine plural: des horaires ___. Both taught plurals are accepted.
practice.explanation: Idéal allows both masculine plural forms.

practice.prompt: Supply glacial in the masculine plural: des vents ___. Both taught plurals are accepted.
practice.explanation: Glacial has two accepted plural forms; glaciaux is common for icy winds.

practice.prompt: Supply mauve as a simple colour after des rubans.
practice.explanation: Mauve is an established agreeing colour adjective.

practice.prompt: Supply pourpre as a simple colour after des capes.
practice.explanation: Pourpre agrees in number.

practice.prompt: Supply écarlate as a simple colour after des tissus.
practice.explanation: Écarlate takes plural s as a variable colour adjective.

practice.prompt: Supply fauve as a simple tawny colour after des vestes.
practice.explanation: Fauve is one of the agreeing colour exceptions.

practice.prompt: Supply incarnat as a simple rosy-red colour after des étoffes. Une étoffe is feminine.
practice.explanation: Incarnat agrees in gender and number: incarnates.

practice.prompt: Supply the mixed shade bleu-vert after des carreaux, retaining the taught compound spelling.
practice.explanation: The mixed compound shade is hyphenated and invariable.

practice.prompt: Supply the compound shade rose pâle after des serviettes.
practice.explanation: Simple rose agrees, but the compound shade rose pâle stays unchanged.

practice.prompt: Supply crème as a colour after des enveloppes.
practice.explanation: Crème is a noun-based colour and remains invariable.

practice.prompt: Form the adverb from énorme: Ces activités me plaisent ___.
practice.explanation: Énormément means a great deal and does not agree with activités.

practice.prompt: Form the adverb from intense: Nous avons travaillé ___ pendant deux jours.
practice.explanation: The learned form is intensément.

practice.prompt: Form the adverb from aveugle: Il ne faut pas suivre les conseils ___.
practice.explanation: Aveuglément means blindly.

practice.prompt: Form the adverb from commun: C'est le terme ___ utilisé.
practice.explanation: Communément means commonly.

practice.prompt: Form the adverb from confus: Je me souviens ___ de cette conversation.
practice.explanation: Confusément can describe a vague or confused recollection.

practice.prompt: Form the adverb from commode meaning conveniently.
practice.explanation: Commode gives commodément, not commodement.

practice.prompt: Form the adverb from conforme: Le dossier a été traité ___ aux règles.
practice.explanation: Conformément à means in accordance with.

practice.prompt: Give the taught adverb related to exprès meaning expressly: Le règlement le prévoit ___.
practice.explanation: Expressément means explicitly or expressly in this context.

practice.prompt: Choose the article for the fixed family term: ___ grands-parents accompagnent les enfants.
practice.explanation: Grands-parents is a fixed noun, so keep the plural indefinite des.

practice.prompt: Write ambigu in the feminine singular for une instruction ___. Both standard diaeresis spellings are accepted.
practice.explanation: The u remains pronounced: traditional ambiguë and rectified ambigüe are both standard.

practice.prompt: Give the feminine plural of aigu for des notes ___, high-pitched notes. Either standard spelling is accepted.
practice.explanation: Retain the pronounced u with a diaeresis and add feminine e and plural s.

practice.prompt: An adjoining room is une salle contiguë or contigüe. Change the adjective to masculine plural for des bureaux ___.
practice.explanation: The masculine has no following e, so it does not need the feminine diaeresis; add plural s to contigu.

practice.prompt: Correct only the spelling of the adjective: Une cabine exigue. Give the adjective alone; either standard diaeresis spelling is accepted.
practice.explanation: The feminine form must preserve the pronounced u with the diaeresis.

practice.prompt: The phrase dépendre de means depend on. Contract de + les only: L'ouverture dépend ___ dernières autorisations.
practice.explanation: This is de + the definite les, not indefinite some. A preceding adjective does not undo the contraction.

practice.prompt: Use the careful-written indefinite article to introduce some new rules: Le règlement contient ___ nouvelles règles.
practice.explanation: Contenir takes a direct object. This is indefinite des before a freely preceding adjective, so use de.

practice.prompt: Supply the single compound shade bleu marine after les couvertures. Give the colour phrase alone.
practice.explanation: A colour qualified by a noun remains invariable as a shade.

practice.prompt: In the taught description des rubans rouge et blanc, what does the invariable colour group describe?
choices: Each ribbon has both red and white.
Some ribbons are entirely red and the others entirely white.
answers: Each ribbon has both red and white.
practice.explanation: The invariable combined colour phrase describes both colours on each ribbon.

practice.prompt: Each marker has both red and white stripes. Supply rouge et blanc after des repères, using either accepted coordinated-colour agreement.
practice.explanation: For objects each bearing several colours, the OQLF accepts both invariable and agreeing coordinated adjectives.

practice.prompt: Form the adverb from uniforme: Les graines doivent être réparties ___ dans les pots.
practice.explanation: Uniformément describes how the seeds are distributed; it does not agree with graines.

production_task.prompt: Describe a room redesign with two agreed adjectives, two colour descriptions (one compound), a plural pre-noun adjective with de/d', and a learned -ément adverb.
production_task.model_answer: Nous avons de nouvelles tables et des sièges originaux. Les rideaux bleu clair vont bien avec les coussins orange. La décoration me plaît énormément. Les formes sont simples et les couleurs sont douces.
production_task.translation: We have new tables and original seats. The light blue curtains go well with the orange cushions. I like the decoration a great deal. The shapes are simple and the colours are soft.
rubric: Check masculine versus feminine plural endings.
Keep the compound shade and the noun-based colour invariable.
Use de before a freely preceding plural adjective.
